Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
330 PM EDT Tue Jul 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Severe Thunderstorm Watch has been issued for the entire area
until 10 PM. A Flash Flood Watch has been issued for the I-64
corridor, Highland, and Pendleton Counties until 2 AM Wednesday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Severe weather risk will continue through this evening with
  the greatest risk across central VA, southern MD, and the 
  Appalachian region. 
  
- Below average temperatures and mainly dry conditions 
  are expected Thursday through the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Severe weather risk will continue through this evening with
the greatest risk across central VA, southern MD, and the Appalachian
region. 

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...

18Z RAOB plots along with WV imagery show an unusually deep
trough across the Great Lks into the OH Valley with an 85-kt 250
mb jet streak measured at Davenport, IA and Wilmington, OH and
55-kt 500 mb wind speeds measured at ILN and IAD. 18Z NUCAPS
data showed the greatest instability and moisture axis resides
along the AKQ and LWX borders. This looks like it will be
battleground zone for the most severe wx and flash flood risk
through this evening into the early morning hours. Multiple 
rounds of thunderstorms are expected, particularly across the 
south where training convection is most likely. Convection 
across OH and southwest PA will have less instability to work 
with, but stronger shear which may still pose a severe wind 
risk. Convection will gradually sink through the evening
tapering from northwest to southeast, but convection will likely
linger along the AKQ and LWX borders well through the night. 

Still a risk of severe wx Wed, but likely for areas south of the
Capital Beltway and southern MD. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Below average temperatures and mainly dry conditions 
are expected Thursday through the weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...

A sprawling area of high pressure will build to our north for 
Thursday and Friday, before shifting off the New England Coastline 
on Saturday. Northerly flow ahead of the approaching high will 
advect a much cooler and drier airmass into the region for Thursday. 
Well below normal temperatures and dewpoints are forecast for late 
July, with high temperatures only in the upper 70s/low 80s. Dewpoints 
in the 50s will also make it feel much less humid than is typical 
for July. Mostly sunny skies will accompany the well below normal 
temperatures/dewpoints. Temperatures will stay well below normal for 
Friday and Saturday within easterly flow. Both temperatures and 
dewpoints begin to rise again on Sunday as flow turns southerly, 
with highs in the mid to upper 80s and dewpoints in the 60s. The 
return of higher dewpoint air should lead to slightly greater 
chances for afternoon/evening showers and thunderstorms, but most 
locations will likely still stay dry.

Forecast confidence decreases substantially by Monday and Tuesday, 
but chances for showers and thunderstorms may further increase as 
multiple shortwave disturbances move through in northwesterly flow 
aloft. Depending on how the forecast details evolve, there could be 
a conditional threat for severe thunderstorms on either Monday or 
Tuesday.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...

Widespread showers and thunderstorms expected through mid
evening with the risk of some severe wx. Thunderstorm risk Wed
will likely stay south of the main terminals. 

Prevailing VFR condtions are expected Thursday through Saturday. 
Winds will generally be out of the north on Thursday, east on 
Friday, and east to southeast on Sunday.

&&

.MARINE...

Numerous to widespread showers and thunderstorms expected, some
of which may require SMWs this afternoon and this evening and
again Wednesday.

SCA conditions may linger in northerly flow into Thursday morning. 
Thereafter, sub-SCA level winds are expected Thursday afternoon 
through Saturday. Winds will generally be out of the north on 
Thursday, east on Friday, and east to southeast on Saturday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Elevated southerly flow continues through this evening, pushing
anomalies close to one foot. No tidal flooding is forecast at
this time, but Annapolis and Havre de Grace will be close. Water
levels will drop as a cold front passes Wednesday.

&&
